news.text: This evaluation dashboard is finally live! It hosts monthly evaluations of the latest AI agents from 7 frontier labs on a fixed core set and newly posted SciConBench samples, measuring their scientific conclusion synthesis capabilities over time.
July 2026 dataset release. The benchmark grows from 9.11K to 9.17K samples; superseded reviews are replaced with their latest editions.
Our paper "Can AI Agents Synthesize Scientific Conclusions?" is on arXiv, introducing SciConBench and SciConHarness, our clean-room evaluation harness.

faq.question: Why does a benchmark need to be live?
faq.answer: Any static benchmark drawn from published literature is already inside the training data of the next model generation. Cochrane publishes new systematic reviews every month, so SciConBench continuously draws fresh questions whose reference conclusions postdate the models being tested. A score here reflects synthesis ability rather than recall of a memorized document.

faq.question: What stops an agent from just finding the answer online?
faq.answer: Every evaluation runs under SciConHarness, a clean-room protocol that proxies web search and page fetching. It filters out the target review, anything citing it, and any source published after the review's date, so the agent has to assemble the conclusion from primary evidence instead of retrieving it. The paper reports that clean-room conditions consistently lower scores relative to unconstrained evaluation, which is direct evidence that leakage inflates estimates of synthesis ability.

faq.question: How are models scored?
faq.answer: Both the agent's conclusion and the expert conclusion are decomposed into atomic facts. Factual precision asks how many of the agent's claims the review supports, penalizing outright contradictions; factual recall measures how many of the expert's claims the agent recovered, treating the Authors' Conclusions section as the authoritative answer. F1 is their harmonic mean, macro-averaged over reviews.

faq.question: How does this dashboard relate to the benchmark on HuggingFace?
faq.answer: The HuggingFace release is the full benchmark: every Cochrane review the pipeline has processed, questions and atomic facts included. This dashboard reports the live evaluation panel, a much smaller set that every tracked model is re-run against each month. The panel combines a frozen core sample, which keeps month-to-month comparisons stable, with each new monthly cohort of freshly published reviews.

faq.question: How do I get a model onto the leaderboard?
faq.answer: Open an issue or pull request on GitHub, or email us. Any model reachable through an OpenAI-, Anthropic-, Gemini-, or OpenRouter-compatible API can be added to the monthly roster in one config change.

faq.question: Can I download the data?
faq.answer: Yes. The benchmark is on HuggingFace as hayoungjung/SciConBench, gated behind a contact-information agreement to keep crawlers from scraping and leaking it. Please do not reshare it in a crawlable format. Cochrane content remains copyrighted by its original authors and Cochrane, and its use is governed by Cochrane and Wiley terms.

introduction: AI agents are transforming how individuals and institutions access and act on scientific knowledge. Unlike traditional search engines that retrieve documents for users to synthesize, these systems increasingly perform the *long-horizon* task of *scientific conclusion synthesis* themselves: retrieving evidence, reasoning across sources, and producing conclusions used in consequential decisions. The stakes are especially high in health, where billions of ChatGPT messages concern healthcare each week and OpenEvidence, a specialized clinical AI copilot for high-stakes decision-making, reports more than 200 million AI-assisted clinical consultations.

*So, can AI agents synthesize scientific conclusions?* **SciConBench** tests this with 9K+ questions paired with expert conclusions from Cochrane systematic reviews. Under **SciConHarness**, agents search and browse the open web through clean-room tools that prevent access to benchmark answers, then assess and integrate evidence into a scientific conclusion evaluated for factual correctness (precision) and completeness (recall). ++The best agent in our preprint reached only 0.337 factual F1.++ Because static benchmarks can leak into models' pretraining data, SciConBench is **live**: each month, we add fresh samples from newly published reviews.

**To track progress in synthesis capability over time, this dashboard evaluates frontier models monthly on fresh samples and a fixed core set, distinguishing capability improvements from gains driven by benchmark leakage.**
